Hi Alice / team —

I’m the infra lead for KMS integrations — quick answers to the questions you raised, plus a few implementation notes so your architects have context before the deep-dive.

1) Supported KMS providers
- AWS KMS (including CloudHSM-backed keys)
- Google Cloud KMS (CloudHSM options where available)
- Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed keys supported)
We provide first-class integrations for these three; others can be evaluated case-by-case.

2) At-rest & in-transit encryption model
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 preferred, TLS 1.2+ supported. Mutual TLS available for private/dedicated endpoints.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM with per-tenant data keys (envelope encryption). Root keys are stored and managed in the customer’s KMS when CMEK/BYOK is enabled.

3) Customer-managed keys (BYOK/CMEK)
- Dedicated & Private: full CMEK support; you can attach your KMS key ARN / resource ID and Redwood will use it as the root key for envelope encryption. Keys are never exported in plaintext from the KMS.
- Hosted (public): we offer an enterprise option that integrates with customer KMS via a VPC-private connector — for most customers we recommend Dedicated/Private if strict CMEK governance is required.

4) Key rotation & lifecycle
- Rotation: supported via KMS rotate-key operations and staged rewrap. We support staged rotation with dual-key acceptance during the rollover window to avoid downtime. For very large model artifacts we provide a background rewrap operation and can coordinate maintenance windows if expedited rewrap is required.
- Deletion/compromise: we follow KMS provider semantics — keys marked for deletion are rejected for new operations and access is removed; we keep audit trails of rewrap/rotate operations. We can run a full rewrap + emergency key rotation plan if required.

5) Exportability & attestation
- Exportability: HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) are non-exportable by design. Our integrations enforce non-exportability for HSM-backed customer keys.
- Attestation: we can provide attestation metadata (FIPS 140-2 validation of the HSM endpoint) and KMS access logs for audit. We will include the relevant artifacts in the SOC 2 package where applicable.

6) Audit & logging
- Access to key usage is logged via the underlying KMS audit logs (CloudTrail / equivalent) and surfaced in Redwood’s console for requests and token-level tracing.

7) Docs & next steps
- KMS integration guide: https://redwood.ai/docs/security#encryption
- Architecture diagram: attached (redwood-kms-architecture-diagram.png)

If this looks good I’ll prepare a short tech appendix describing step-by-step how to register your AWS KMS key and how we handle rotation. I’ll also join Tue 2026-02-24 9:30am PT for the deep-dive.
